frozen_R5_priority: An active (in-flight) non-Exception BaseException primary is never replaced by any cleanup, diagnostic, report, retention, emission or bookkeeping failure. With no primary or an ordinary-Exception primary, the FIRST eligible newly arising non-Exception BaseException (in arising order: close outcome, then its diagnostic, then sweep bookkeeping) propagates only after every remaining owned single attempt. Ordinary cleanup errors are latched and returned; an ordinary primary is preserved; without any primary a failed direct close fails its own operation. This is NOT the PRT newest-origin rule and nothing from PRT is copied.

planned_change: Delete _secondary (its unprotected latch.append and the unprotected lambda construction at every call site).

New _secondary_failed(emergency, failure): sets the preallocated emergency['failed'] flag first (allocation-free), then appends type(failure).__name__ to the bounded (DIAG_ROWS) emergency['types'] list inside its own try; never raises (used only while a non-Exception primary is in flight).

run() preallocates emergency = {'failed': False, 'types': []} before bootstrap; the bootstrap BaseException handler and _base_exception_line perform report, report retention and compact emission each inside its own try/except BaseException -> _secondary_failed, with cleanup in finally.

Reader retention under the primary becomes one preallocated slot ctx.emergency_reader (set in _Context.__init__), replacing the unprotected retained_exception_readers.append; case-owned appends (RD08C/SC33/AD36, normal flow) are unchanged.

Cleanup under the primary goes through _cleanup_under(owned, index, primary): close_since inside try; any escaping fault sets owned.uncertain and is re-raised only if it is a non-Exception over an ordinary primary (R5).

planned_change: _Owned gains allocation-free latches uncertain and diagnostics_incomplete; rows gain a preallocated diagnostic_failure key; new _close_once(row) performs the single native close and never raises: on failure it sets owned.uncertain and stores the actual exception in row['close_error'] BEFORE any repr/list growth, then appends a bounded (DIAG_ROWS=16 rows, DIAG_CHARS=200 characters) best-effort diagnostic inside its own try whose failure sets diagnostics_incomplete and is kept in row['diagnostic_failure'].

_Owned.close(row, primary): one attempt via _close_once; raises the first eligible non-Exception event (close error, then diagnostic failure) as _escalates allows, else the ordinary close error only when there is no primary at all, else returns the error. Direct _Fx finalizers are unchanged and now cannot be replaced by diagnostics.

_Owned.close_since: every remaining row gets its single attempt; events collected in arising order (close error, diagnostic failure); a sweep bookkeeping fault is latched, counted as an event and resumed once by a second sweep that skips attempted rows; if both sweeps fault the latch stays set; the first eligible non-Exception event is raised only after the sweeps; the first error is returned otherwise.

_FaultOS replaces the violations list by the allocation-free flag violated (the list was never output; only its emptiness fed accounting_ok); every violation site sets the flag; records gain cleanup_error; new _clear_one(rec) performs the identity-checked single close and never raises (latch first, actual exception kept on the record, no fallible diagnostic); clear_orphans sweeps like close_since and raises the first eligible non-Exception event after every record.

Every exit/refusal decision reads owned.uncertain instead of owned.errors (bootstrap 1653/1694/1699, exit selection 1790, final close 1812); owned.errors remains a bounded best-effort diagnostic in summaries.
_escalates stays the frozen rule function, unchanged; exception handlers use its allocation-free inline equivalent for non-Exception events.

planned_change: run() preallocates outcome = {'deadline': False, 'budget': False, 'error': False}; new _classify(outcome, failure) maps HarnessDeadlineExceeded -> deadline, HarnessBudgetExceeded -> budget, any other Exception -> error.

Case emission: one except Exception handler classifies the failure; deadline/budget keep the v4 stop statuses, any other ordinary failure makes the case status ERROR (undelivered record); one compact fallback line is attempted inside its own try and its failure is classified, never escaping.

Finalization: protected-state reads, provisional summary persistence, final close_since(0) and final summary emission are each classified; summary status/exit_code are recomputed by _summary_status; the exit code comes from one fixed precedence _code: deadline 5 > budget 6 > error/mismatch/ownership/protected/undelivered 3 > inconclusive 4 > 0.

Run-level except Exception after bootstrap: classify, _cleanup_under(owned, 0, failure), observe the deadline, emit one minimal summary only if no summary line was delivered, observe the deadline again, return the classified nonzero code; non-Exception BaseExceptions keep propagating after cleanup.
_emit reserves stdout bytes before the write (a failed or partial write still counts toward the 1 MiB bound) and records summary delivery in output_state['summary'].
New _late(deadline): original-deadline observation for finalization phases; an unreadable clock counts as crossed.

Pre-case refusal: code 5 for HarnessDeadlineExceeded else 7; close_since(0) guarded (bookkeeping fault latches uncertainty; a non-Exception event still propagates per R5); deadline re-observed after cleanup (code 5) and after the refusal summary (return 5); refusal-summary delivery failure cannot change 7/5; diagnostic text bounded to DIAG_CHARS.
